subject: Headroom coverage & GPU allocation for renewal - OlderA
messages:
From: Emma Lin <emma.lin@oldera.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@oldera.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + required headroom for Q1 launch

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the renewal draft. We're targeting a product relaunch in Q1 that will increase traffic to our inference endpoints. Attached is our Q3 usage export (summary + hourly breakdown). Quick asks: can Redwood guarantee a throughput floor for burst windows and advise how many extra GPUs we should reserve to cover peak growth + 30% headroom?

Right now on the Dedicated pool we average ~120 QPS (p50) for our low-latency route with avg request = 950 tokens in/out. We expect a phased growth to ~200 QPS over the next 9–12 months with a conservative 25% day-of-event surge.

We want a recommended reserved count and a proposal for a 12-month committed term (including burst buffer and an SLA for 99p latency). Can you and your team map this to a suggested reserve plan and cost estimate?

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Lin
Head of ML Platform, OlderA Systems
(attachment: oldera_q3_usage.csv (csv))

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@oldera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + required headroom for Q1 launch

Emma — thanks for the data, attached a short read + quick model. High level summary up front: to cover steady growth to ~200 QPS and allow for a 25–30% surge day-of-event while maintaining your 99p latency SLO (~<300ms for short responses), we recommend increasing your reserved pool from 8 GPUs to 14 GPUs (add 6 GPUs).

Rationale (brief):
- Baseline: current 8x A100-80Gb equiv handles ~120 QPS with average generation length ~950 tokens.
- Forecast: we model 200 QPS steady-state in 9–12 months; adding 6 GPUs provides ~52–60% capacity uplift which covers steady growth + 30% surge buffer when combined with our burst capacity rules.
- Throughput mapping: we used observed per-GPU throughput of ~15–18 QPS (median) for your model mix (multi-turn chat + generation). For peak short requests (<=256 tokens) per-GPU throughput increases; for long-tail requests (>=2k tokens) throughput drops — we included request mix.

Recommended term & protections:
- 12-month reserved commitment for 14 GPUs with a monthly burst allowance: additional ephemeral 2 GPUs for up to 6 hours/day during pre-announced events.
- SLA: 99.9% availability for the reserved pool; SLO for 99th percentile latency on low-latency route: <=300ms (we'll list compatible model variants).
- Pricing: illustrative: 30% discount off on-demand for the committed GPUs, + nominal fee for guaranteed burst slots. Full pricing in attached PDF.

Next steps: Marissa will run a quick cost sensitivity across a +/-2 GPU swing and then we can share a formal amendment to the renewal. Ben — can you sign off on the burst wording and confirm the SLA language?

Attaching: redwood_headroom_proposal_20261013.pdf

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_headroom_proposal_20261013.pdf (pdf))

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + required headroom for Q1 launch

Couple of practical knobs I ran through the model:

- If OlderA is comfortable with a 10% higher request batching (we can enable micro-batching for non-low-latency routes), they could keep 12 GPUs (add 4) and still hit effective throughput for most daytime traffic. That reduces monthly committed cost ~8–10%.
- Quantization profile: switching 2 of the 14 GPUs to INT8-backed variants for background rerank jobs saves compute and reduces hot-seat contention. We call this a split-pool approach in the amendment.
- We should offer a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent of ~0.5 GPU-month) if they sign the 12-month commitment within 21 days.

Ben, confirm the burst SLA phrasing + whether two ephemeral GPUs can be announced with a 48-hour notice (instead of pre-announced window). If we do 48-hour notice, cost impact is negligible and gives their ops room.

Marissa
Director, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Emma Lin <emma.lin@oldera.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + required headroom for Q1 launch

Emma / team — looping in final legal-friendly language and confirming operational commitments. Agreed items:

- Reserved pool: 14 GPUs (8 existing + 6 added) under a 12-month commitment.
- Burst buffer: up to 2 ephemeral GPUs for up to 6 hours/day with 48-hour notice; can increase for one-off events with pre-paid burst credits.
- SLA: Reserved pool availability 99.9%; 99p latency objective for your low-latency route <=300ms. Formal SLA and credits spelled out in amendment.
- Pricing: 30% off on-demand for reserved GPUs; split-pool quantization options described by Marissa are included as optional items.

I'll follow up with an amendment draft and an updated pricing worksheet. Priya/Marissa — please include a short paragraph that explains the modeling assumptions (per-GPU QPS range, token mix, surge factor) so OlderA's procurement team can see the math.

Best,
Ben Carter
VP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood_headroom_proposal_20261020.pdf (pdf))
